subject: literature
passage: On the last afternoon, Mr. Abernathy did not teach. He had prepared a lesson, as he had for thirty-eight years, and it lay on his desk in his small, upright hand; but when the boys had settled he found he did not want to give it. He asked instead what they remembered. There was the silence he knew well, in which forty boys wait to see who will be brave, and then a thin boy at the back said he remembered the day the stove had smoked and they had done Latin in their coats. Another remembered a map. A third remembered being told, kindly, that he was wrong. <u>None of them mentioned anything that Mr. Abernathy would have called the substance of his teaching, and he was surprised to find that this did not grieve him.</u> He gathered his papers and let them go early.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It reveals that the boys had deliberately avoided mentioning the lessons in order to tease their teacher.
choices.B: It suggests that the teacher regrets having spent his career on lessons that his students have forgotten.
choices.C: It notes a gap between what the teacher valued in his work and what his students retained, and registers his unexpected response to that gap.
choices.D: It explains why the teacher decided not to give the lesson he had prepared.

explanation.why: The boys' memories (the smoking stove, a map, a kind correction) are all incidental to the lessons themselves. The underlined sentence names that gap directly, noting that none of the memories concern "the substance of his teaching," and then records the teacher's unexpected reaction: it "did not grieve him." The sentence thus states the contrast the examples have built and gives the emotional turn of the passage.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the boys were teasing; their memories are offered sincerely after a nervous silence.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence says explicitly that the discovery "did not grieve him."
explanation.C: Correct. The sentence observes that the memories miss the "substance" of the teaching and then reports his surprise at not minding.
explanation.D: Incorrect. His decision not to teach comes at the start and is left unexplained; the underlined sentence is about the boys' answers.
